lessons.title: Scope, Focus, and Implication
lessons.learn: Distinguish assertion, presupposition, and invited inference through focus and lexical precision.

grammar.title: Focus and semantic scope
grammar.explain: Focus markers restrict alternatives; their position changes what is excluded. A C2 speaker can state which proposition was asserted and which conclusion remains inferential.

lessons.title: Counterfactual Viewpoint and Evidential Distance
lessons.learn: Manipulate tense and mood to locate responsibility, regret, probability, and unreal alternatives.

grammar.title: Compound conditionals and viewpoint
grammar.explain: The pluperfect subjunctive plus conditional perfect constructs an unreal past. Evidential futures and conditionals can mark probability or reported distance rather than time alone.

lessons.title: Rhetoric, Irony, and Ethical Persuasion

grammar.title: Rhetorical stance

grammar.pattern: fair objection → concession → rebuttal → proportionate proposal

grammar.title: Deontic modality and agency

grammar.title: Invariant content across genres
grammar.explain: Style changes density, interpersonal force, and terminology; it must not silently change conditions, dissent, or evidential status.

examples.t: Aceptaremos la propuesta con la condición de que la revisión sea independiente.
examples.r: aseptaremos la propuesta kon la kondisyon de ke la revision sea independyente
examples.en: We will accept the proposal provided the review is independent.

examples.t: El acta hará constar que dos partes mantuvieron su desacuerdo.
examples.r: el akta ara konstar ke dos partes mantuvyeron su desakwerdo
examples.en: The minutes will record that two parties maintained their disagreement.

examples.t: La versión pública explicará la condición sin presentarla como consenso pleno.
examples.r: la versyon publika explikara la kondisyon sin presentarla komo konsenso pleno
examples.en: The public version will explain the condition without presenting it as full consensus.

mistakes: Preserve mood, stance, cohesion, and register; a grammatically possible form may still be pragmatically inappropriate.
